full_judgment: 2. In this matter, the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 instituted the suit praying for a decree for declaration that the letter No. BHMMA- 23/2002/184 dated 19-10-2002, issued by the defendant No. 2 to the plaintiff No. 2 is illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs, contending, inter alia, that they are the elected president and vice president of the Khulna Circle of the Bangladesh Hardware Machinery Merchants Association ('Association' in short) for the term 2000 to 2002, that the defendant Nos. 3 to 5 misused power and funds of the organisation, that they tried to victimise the plaintiffs, that the defendants hatched up a conspiracy and managed to issue the letter No. BHMMA-II/02/140 dated 17-8-2002, that in furtherance of their conspiracy the defendants issued the impugned letter dated 19-10- 2002 by which the plaintiffs were suspended from their posts of president and vice president of the Khulna Circle of the aforesaid organisation. On receipt of the notice of the suit the petitioner Nos. 1 and 3 (defendant Nos. 3 and 5) and the petitioner No. 2 (defendant No. 4) filed two separate applications under Order VII rule 11 (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, contending, inter alia, that the Association is a registered trade organisation and the plaintiff being a member of the said organisation, challenged the decision of the organisation in the suit which is barred under section 12 of the Trade Organisation Ordinance, 1961. The learned Judge in his order No. 6, dated 19-11-2002, observed that under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Civil Court has got jurisdiction to try all kinds of suits of civil nature and since the instant suit is civil in nature, he rejected the said application under Order VII rule 11of the Code of Civil Procedure, relying on the decision of the Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Commerce vs Nizamuddin Haider 1985 BLD 57, held that in spite of express ouster of jurisdiction, the Civil Court has got jurisdiction to examine whether the impugned action has been taken illegally or in excess of jurisdiction. The learned Judge further held that the forum of arbitration provided by section 12(2) of the Trade Organisation Ordinance, 1961, is not suitable in the present case. On the same day, by a separate order No. 7 dated 19-11-2002, he granted temporary injunction and restrained the defendants from obstructing the plaintiffs in performing their functions till disposal of the suit.
